our_interpretation: The plain reading is that growing machine-generated misinformation will substantially outstrip the human-led system’s ability to provide timely corrections.
Coverage and response time are my operational measures; Marcus supplied neither a numerical threshold nor a deadline.
The condition requires observed growth in machine-generated misleading content, not merely improvements in AI capabilities.
Introducing AI note writers is not, by itself, proof that the earlier system was overwhelmed.
criteria.support_condition: After the condition occurs, sustained measurements show that the mostly manual system substantially fails to keep pace with machine-generated misinformation in correction coverage or timeliness.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative measurements showing sustained, timely and broad correction by the mostly manual system during accelerating machine-generated misinformation would contradict failure during that episode. Temporary success cannot conclusively refute an unlimited future forecast.

evidence.explanation: The analysis through January 2026 reports an upward trajectory and recent acceleration in AI-generated visual misinformation captured by Community Notes. This supports occurrence of the condition within the observed sample, without establishing platform-wide prevalence.

The selected AI posts received slower initial annotations but had stronger subsequent agreement, providing evidence both of delay and continuing capacity. The study’s consensus measure includes Helpful and Not Helpful decisions; it does not establish visible correction coverage or sustained overload.

The platform team reports that AI writers extended coverage while humans continued to rate notes. This documents adaptation, but neither proves earlier overload nor measures how an unchanged manual system would have performed.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A dated longitudinal study measuring AI misinformation volume, visible correction coverage and delays, with human and AI contributions separated, could establish that the manual system was substantially overtaken. A deadline would be needed to conclusively reject eventual failure based only on continued success.
